description: THE HEADLINE HAPPY PATH - the complete bill payment, end to end, on production-shaped fixture data. WHEN 'Y' at app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:174 of the ordered EVALUATE CONFIRMI at :173-191, and the only case in this directory that reaches :211-235 in full: the cross-reference is read, the master is browsed backwards, the 350-byte transaction is assembled and ADDED, and only THEN is the balance reduced and the account rewritten. SERVICE. This case defines the canonical written-record images that its siblings reference, so every span of both records is pinned twice - once as a named field and once inside the complete image. IN SOURCE ORDER, AND THE ORDER IS THE BEHAVIOUR. :156 SET CONF-PAY-NO TO TRUE, before any validation. :158-167 EVALUATE TRUE finds ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI non-blank, so it takes WHEN OTHER / CONTINUE at :165-166 - a genuine no-op arm, and no error flag. :169 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON opens and :170-171 MOVE ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI TO ACCT-ID / XREF-ACCT-ID: ONE MOVE WITH TWO RECEIVERS, a PIC X(11) sending item into two PIC 9(11) items, and there is NO NUMERIC VALIDATION ANYWHERE IN THIS PROGRAM. None is added here (practice B5). One statement fills both keys, which is why the account read at :177 and the cross-reference read at :211 address the same identifier without a second move between them. :173-191 then evaluates CONFIRMI in exact source order: WHEN 'Y' at :174 MATCHES, so WHEN 'y' at :175 shares its body, and WHEN 'N' at :178, WHEN 'n' at :179, WHEN SPACES at :182, WHEN LOW-VALUES at :183 and WHEN OTHER at :185 are never reached. EVALUATE takes the FIRST matching WHEN and WHEN OTHER is the default, so an implementation that reordered the arms or let one fall through into the next would be a different program (gate G30). :176 SET CONF-PAY-YES TO TRUE is the statement the whole case turns on: it is the only thing that makes :210 take its IF rather than its ELSE, and it is the entire distinction between this case and the lookup-and-prompt of case10. THE READ IS ISSUED WITH UPDATE. :177 performs READ-ACCTDAT-FILE, which at :345-354 is EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-ACCTDAT-FILE) INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCOUNT-RECORD) RIDFLD(ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCT-ID) UPDATE RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), and the EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :356-372 takes its first arm, WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :357, whose body is CONTINUE. In Java that is AccountRepository.readForUpdate and the record is HELD until the REWRITE at :235 replaces it - the one path in the program where the UPDATE option is actually used for what it is for (gate G47). WS-ACCTDAT-FILE is 'ACCTDAT ' at :41; the dataset is addressed here by the binding key ACCTDAT that src/main/resources/application-test.yml declares, never by a literal dataset name. THE EDITED BALANCE. :193 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO WS-CURR-BAL and :194 MOVE WS-CURR-BAL TO CURBALI OF COBIL0AI run inside the :169 guard and outside the EVALUATE, so they fire on this arm too and leave +0000000194.00 in CURBALI. WS-CURR-BAL is PIC +9999999999.99 at :56 - a sign position, ten integer positions, an actual decimal point character and two fraction positions, which is fourteen bytes and an exact fit for the symbolic map's CURBALI PIC X(14) at app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:66. THOSE FOURTEEN CHARACTERS ARE NOT WHAT THE SENDS CARRY, and that is not a contradiction: :524 blanks the field again before either send happens. The edited image is asserted where it survives, on case10's send; here it is transient, and pinning it would assert a screen the program never transmits. STAGE THREE PASSES, STAGE FOUR PAYS. :197-206 tests IF ACCT-CURR-BAL <= ZEROS AND ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES - a conjunction - and the balance just read is 194.00, above zero, so 'You have nothing to pay...' does not fire and no flag is raised. :208 opens the last guard and :210 IF CONF-PAY-YES is TRUE. THE CROSS-REFERENCE READ, AND WHY IT IS A FINDER AND NOT A TABLE. :211 performs READ-CXACAIX-FILE, which at :410-418 is EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-CXACAIX-FILE) INTO(CARD-XREF-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF CARD-XREF-RECORD) RIDFLD(XREF-ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF XREF-ACCT-ID) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) - note the ABSENCE of UPDATE, because nothing rewrites this record - and the EVALUATE at :420-436 takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :421 / CONTINUE (gate G47). app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines CXACAIX with DESCRIPTION(ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY) and DSNAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH): it is a PATH over the CCXREF base cluster, not a dataset of its own, so in Java it is ONE repository with a second finder - CardXrefRepository.readByAccountIdViaAltIndex on the eleven-byte alternate key - and never a second table (gate G45). The row it returns supplies XREF-CARD-NUM for the move at :225 and nothing else; the record is read and never written, which is why the cross-reference appears in inputs and in normalisations and in NEITHER expectedWrites nor expectedFinalState nor expectedDatasets. THE CROSS-REFERENCE ROW INDEX IS 48, AND IT WAS COMPUTED, NOT ASSUMED. app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt is ordered by its BASE KEY, XREF-CARD-NUM ASCENDING - row 0 is card 0500024453765740 / customer 000000050 / account 00000000050 - so the zero-based row index for an account is emphatically NOT accountNumber minus one. All fifty account identifiers 00000000001 through 00000000050 are present, exactly one row each; slicing bytes 26-36 of every row locates 00000000001 at ZERO-BASED ROW 48, carrying customer 000000001 and card 9680294154603697, which is the value TRAN-CARD-NUM receives. AND THE FIXTURE IS SEEDED AT 36 BYTES, DELIBERATELY UNPADDED. app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares fifty - XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) at 1-16, XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) at 17-25, XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) at 26-36 and FILLER X(14) at 37-50 - and the fixture omits that trailing FILLER, making it the one fixture of the nine that is not faithful to its copybook (gate G16, risk R-F). ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow is the declared SOLE OWNER of the 36-to-50 right-pad, applied once at SEED time through the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation this case declares against CXACAIX. Pre-padding the rows here would double-apply it and produce a 64-byte row, so the rows are left exactly as the fixture stores them. HIGH-VALUES, THE BROWSE, AND THE BARE ENDBR. :212 MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO TRAN-ID fills the PIC X(16) key with sixteen bytes of the highest value the collating sequence has, which under the explicitly named US-ASCII code page of the nine fixtures is 0xFF sixteen times - the figurative constant, not the literal characters 'HIGH-VALUES'. It is recorded rather than encoded, because what CICS does with a high-values RIDFLD is 'position past the last record', and an UNANCHORED BACKWARD BROWSE expresses that in a way any code page can carry; that is why no key literal appears in the expectation. :213 performs STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE, whose EVALUATE at :451-467 takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :452 / CONTINUE, and :214 performs READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE, whose EVALUATE at :484-496 takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :485 / CONTINUE and leaves the HIGHEST-keyed row in TRAN-RECORD (gate G47). The master is seeded with exactly one row so that arm is the one taken; the WHEN DFHRESP(ENDFILE) arm at :487-488, which instead does MOVE ZEROS TO TRAN-ID, is a sibling case's subject and is deliberately not reached here. :215 performs ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE, which at :503-505 is a BARE EXEC CICS ENDBR DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) WITH NO RESP OPTION, NO RESP2 AND NO EVALUATE OF ANY KIND. That absence is preserved and not repaired (practice B5): no failure arm is invented for it, and the expectation records no outcome for it, because the program observes none. THE IDENTIFIER ARITHMETIC. :216 MOVE TRAN-ID TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM moves PIC X(16) into the PIC 9(16) at :57 - a cross-representation move at EQUAL width, so no digit is lost - and :217 ADD 1 TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM is the program's only non-monetary arithmetic. The seeded master holds 0000000000000007, so the sum is 0000000000000007 + 1 = 0000000000000008: the increment lands entirely in the UNITS position, with no carry into any higher digit and nowhere near the sixteen-nines boundary where a PIC 9(16) receiver with no ON SIZE ERROR clause would discard its high-order digit and wrap to zeros. The identifier is therefore unambiguous, and it is the value :219 moves into TRAN-ID and :529 strings into the confirmation. THE 350-BYTE RECORD, SUMMED FROM app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy RATHER THAN FROM PROSE (practice B11). TRAN-ID X(16) at 1-16, TRAN-TYPE-CD X(02) at 17-18, TRAN-CAT-CD 9(04) at 19-22, TRAN-SOURCE X(10) at 23-32, TRAN-DESC X(100) at 33-132, TRAN-AMT S9(09)V99 at 133-143, TRAN-MERCHANT-ID 9(09) at 144-152, TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) at 153-202, TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) at 203-252, TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) at 253-262, TRAN-CARD-NUM X(16) at 263-278, TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26) at 279-304, TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) at 305-330 and FILLER X(20) at 331-350. That is 350, the RECLN the copybook's own header states (gate G19). :218 INITIALIZE TRAN-RECORD first - alphanumerics to spaces, numerics to zero - and then the eleven moves at :219-229 in source order, which is NOT copybook order: :225 moves TRAN-CARD-NUM before :226 moves TRAN-MERCHANT-ID, while the copybook declares the merchant identifier, name, city and zip ahead of the card number. The field map below is in COPYBOOK DECLARATION ORDER, because that is the order the record's bytes are in and the order a field-for-field diff walks. Three of the spans are cross-width alphanumeric moves and each pads on the RIGHT: 'POS TERM' into X(10) leaves two trailing spaces, the 21-character 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE' into X(100) leaves 79, 'BILL PAYMENT' into X(50) leaves 38, and 'N/A' leaves 47 in the city and 7 in the zip. TRAN-CAT-CD receives the numeric literal 2 into PIC 9(04) and is ZERO-FILLED ON THE LEFT to 0002 - the opposite direction from the alphanumerics, which is the whole reason the two are not interchangeable - and TRAN-MERCHANT-ID receives 999999999 into PIC 9(09) exactly. FILLER X(20) IS PINNED, AS TWENTY SPACES (gate G21): it is an addressable span and not a gap, and omitting it would make the image 330 bytes and shift nothing after it because there is nothing after it - which is precisely why the total width is the only thing that can catch its absence, and why the complete image is pinned alongside the fourteen named fields. THE LEFT-TRUNCATING MOVE AT :224 - THIS PROGRAM'S NUMERIC TRAP. MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO TRAN-AMT moves PIC S9(10)V99 (TEN integer digits, twelve character positions) into PIC S9(09)V99 (NINE integer digits, eleven positions). A numeric receiver is aligned on its IMPLIED DECIMAL POINT, so a numeric MOVE truncates on the LEFT and the digit that does not fit is the HIGH-ORDER one - the exact opposite of the alphanumeric moves above, which truncate on the right. FOR THIS CASE'S BALANCE OF 194.00 THE MOVE IS LOSSLESS: 194.00 needs three integer digits and nine are available, so TRAN-AMT receives 194.00 intact and the subtraction at :234 yields EXACTLY 0.00. That is stated rather than assumed, because the move is NOT always lossless: a balance at or above 1,000,000,000.00 loses its high-order digit, the amount paid is a billion short of the balance, and the residual balance is NON-ZERO. That lossy shape is sibling case20's subject and is not silently generalised from here. THE 26-BYTE TIMESTAMP, DERIVED AND THEN PINNED. :230 performs GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP at :249-267: EXEC CICS ASKTIME ABSTIME(WS-ABS-TIME) at :251-253, then EXEC CICS FORMATTIME at :255-261 ABSTIME(WS-ABS-TIME) YYYYMMDD(WS-CUR-DATE-X10) DATESEP('-') TIME(WS-CUR-TIME-X08) TIMESEP(':'), then INITIALIZE WS-TIMESTAMP, MOVE WS-CUR-DATE-X10 TO WS-TIMESTAMP(01:10), MOVE WS-CUR-TIME-X08 TO WS-TIMESTAMP(12:08) and MOVE ZEROS TO WS-TIMESTAMP-TM-MS6. app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy declares WS-TIMESTAMP as 9(04) + FILLER '-' + 9(02) + FILLER '-' + 9(02) + FILLER ' ' + 9(02) + FILLER ':' + 9(02) + FILLER ':' + 9(02) + FILLER '.' + 9(06), which sums to 26 with separators at bytes 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20. THE DERIVATION THAT MATTERS: IBM COBOL's INITIALIZE does NOT touch FILLER items, so all six separators SURVIVE the INITIALIZE; bytes 1-10 are then overwritten with YYYY-MM-DD, bytes 12-19 with HH:MM:SS, and bytes 21-26 with 000000. BYTE 20 IS THEREFORE A PERIOD - not a space and not a digit - and the microseconds are ALWAYS 000000, because the MOVE ZEROS at :266 is unconditional and nothing in the program ever writes a sub-second value. The image is 2022-07-19 23:12:32.000000, exactly 26 characters. :231-232 MOVE WS-TIMESTAMP TO TRAN-ORIG-TS TRAN-PROC-TS is ONE MOVE WITH TWO RECEIVERS, both PIC X(26), so TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS hold the IDENTICAL twenty-six bytes: this program has no separate processing time, and a translation that derived the second from a second clock reading would differ here. DETERMINISM. The instant is PINNED to 2022-07-19T23:12:32 - the instant the program's own version footer at :571 carries, and the same instant every other case in this directory pins - and it is supplied by the injected Clock that common/DateHeader reads, never by a captured now (practice B7). A captured timestamp would make this case pass once and fail on the next run, and it would poison two spans of the written record and both derived header renderings at once. Two-digit month, day and hour, no midnight and no daylight-saving edge, so the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS header renderings POPULATE-HEADER-INFO derives from the same instant - 07/19/22 and 23:12:32 - are unambiguous and mutually consistent with the 26-byte image above. Those six header items are POPULATE-HEADER-INFO's at :319-338 and belong to BillPaymentController rather than to the service under test, so a SERVICE case does not claim them; case01 and case03 pin all ten items of the map. US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, which for a nine-fixture ASCII corpus and a twelve-dataset EBCDIC one is the difference between a comparison and a coincidence (practice B8). WRITE, THEN COMPUTE, THEN REWRITE - AND THE ORDER IS PINNED. :233 PERFORM WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE, :234 COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT, :235 PERFORM UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE, in that sequence and no other. THE CONSEQUENCE IS OBSERVABLE AND IS THE MOST LIKELY MISREADING OF THIS PROGRAM: the transaction is written with TRAN-AMT equal to the PRE-PAYMENT balance of 194.00, and the balance only becomes 0.00 afterwards. A translation that reduced the balance first would write TRAN-AMT as 0.00 and would be a different program. The order is asserted structurally as well as by value - expectedWrites carries the TRANSACT record at write position 0 and the ACCTDAT record at write position 0 of its own dataset, and expectedDatasets states one row on each WRITES channel - so a reversal cannot pass. THE SINGLE COMPUTE, AND WHY IT TRUNCATES. :234 is the ONLY COMPUTE in COBIL00C's 572 lines and one of the 32 COMPUTE sites in the codebase, so it carries a targeted assertion (gate G28). It has NO ROUNDED phrase - and the keyword ROUNDED appears ZERO TIMES across all 28 programs, verified - so COBOL TRUNCATES excess fractional digits on store. In Java the subtraction is exact and the store is BigDecimal.setScale at SCALE 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN, which CobolDecimal names and nothing else does. HALF_UP, HALF_EVEN, CEILING and FLOOR ARE ALL WRONG (gate G24, AAP rule R2). Both operands and the receiver are scale 2 - a V-scale scan of all 28 copybooks returns only V99 (gate G23) - and neither is ever a double or a float (AAP rule R4). 194.00 minus 194.00 is exactly 0.00 at scale 2, so no rounding decision is actually exercised on this path; the mode is named because it is the rule that governs the store, and because a sibling case whose remainder is non-zero depends on this case having stated it. There is NO COMP-3 IN ANY COPYBOOK IN THIS REPOSITORY - verified zero - so no packed-decimal nibble unpacking is involved anywhere in the record layer; the WS-ABS-TIME PIC S9(15) COMP-3 at :59 is working storage and is never persisted. ZONED DECIMAL, AND WHY THE BYTES ARE PINNED RATHER THAN THE QUANTITY. A signed DISPLAY item occupies exactly p + s character positions and the sign consumes none of its own, overpunched instead into the TRAILING byte; that is the only reading under which CVACT01Y sums to 300 and CVTRA05Y to 350. TRAN-AMT is therefore the eleven bytes 0000001940{ - the digits 00000019400, whose first nine are the integer part 000000194 and whose last two are the fraction 00, with '{' being a positive sign carrying a low-order digit of zero - so the value is 194.00 and not 1940.00. ACCT-CURR-BAL in the rewritten row is the twelve bytes 00000000000{, eleven zero digits and the '{' overpunch: a POSITIVE zero, which is a different byte from the '}' of a negative zero and from the '0' of the unsigned rendering. Pinning the stored image rather than a decimal literal pins the OVERPUNCH BYTE ITSELF, and the unsigned form 000000000000 decodes to the same quantity while not being what COBOL writes into a signed DISPLAY item. THE SUCCESS ARM, IN SOURCE ORDER, AND THE SCREEN IT LEAVES BLANK. :512-520 is EXEC CICS WRITE DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) FROM(TRAN-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-RECORD) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), and the EVALUATE at :522-547 takes its first arm, WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :523 (gate G47). Its body runs in this order and the order is the point. :524 PERFORM INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS runs FIRST, and at :560-566 that paragraph is MOVE -1 TO ACTIDINL at :562 followed by one MOVE SPACES with FOUR RECEIVERS - ACTIDINI, CURBALI, CONFIRMI and WS-MESSAGE - each blanked at its own declared width. SO THE SUCCESSFUL SCREEN SHOWS A BLANK ACCOUNT IDENTIFIER (eleven spaces), A BLANK BALANCE (fourteen spaces) AND A BLANK CONFIRMATION (one space), even though the record's balance was just updated: the fields the user typed are cleared for the next payment, and populating them would assert a screen the program does not send. Note what is NOT blanked - ERRMSGO, which keeps whatever the last send put there until the next send overwrites it, which is exactly what lets this arm blank WS-MESSAGE and then compose a confirmation into it. :525 MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE, and it is not redundant: STRING overlays from the receiver's first byte and does NOT blank the tail, so without :525 the confirmation would be written over whatever was there. The cursor is ACTIDINL, from that MOVE -1 at :562; -1 is CURSOR METADATA and not payload - an xxxL length item is how COBOL positions the cursor - so it is declared as cursorField and not as a screen field. THE COLOUR. :526 MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC OF COBIL0AO is the ONLY attribute assignment anywhere in COBIL00C's 572 lines, and it overrides the COLOR=RED that app/bms/COBIL00.bms declares as ERRMSG's default - the message line turns green precisely once, on success. It is recorded as HIGHLIGHT METADATA in the attributes map and not as a payload field, because ERRMSGC is an attribute item of the COBIL0AO group and carries no text. DFHBMSCA is IBM-supplied and ABSENT from this repository (risk R-D), so the mnemonic comes from common/BmsAttributes, the single reproduction of it, rather than from a copybook; DFHAID is absent for the same reason, which is where the DFHENTER mnemonic comes from. Nothing in the program ever clears ERRMSGC - the only statement that resets the output map is the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COBIL0AO of first entry, and this is a re-entry - so BOTH sends carry the green attribute. THIS IS THE ENTIRETY OF GATE G38's HIGHLIGHT FOR THIS PROGRAM. COBIL00C copies NEITHER CSSETATY NOR CSSTRPFY, and DFHRED appears nowhere in its 572 lines, so there is no red-and-asterisk field marking to assert and none is invented. THE CONFIRMATION TEXT, COUNTED CHARACTER BY CHARACTER. :527-531 is STRING 'Payment successful. ' DELIMITED BY SIZE ' Your Transaction ID is ' DELIMITED BY SIZE TRAN-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE '.' DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO WS-MESSAGE. Both literals are DELIMITED BY SIZE, so each contributes EVERY character it has including the TRAILING space of the first and the LEADING space of the second - which is why TWO CONSECUTIVE SPACES separate 'successful.' from 'Your'. TRAN-ID is DELIMITED BY SPACE, which takes the characters up to but not including the first space; a sixteen-digit zero-padded identifier contains no space, so ALL SIXTEEN DIGITS contribute. The result is exactly 'Payment successful.  Your Transaction ID is 0000000000000008.' - 20 + 24 + 16 + 1 = 61 characters. :293 then moves the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE over the 78-byte ERRMSGO, so the value asserted on each send is those 61 characters left-justified and space-padded to exactly 78; the two-byte loss is the picture difference between PIC X(80) and PIC X(78) and not a shortened expectation, and with 19 spaces to spare nothing of the text is actually cut. TWO SENDS, ONE MESSAGE, AND WHERE THEY ARE RECORDED. :532 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN is send #1, from inside the WRITE's success arm. Control then returns to :234 and :235, and :242 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN fires again UNCONDITIONALLY - it sits after the END-IF at :240, so it runs on both halves of the :210 branch - which is send #2. WS-MESSAGE still holds the confirmation and ERRMSGC still holds DFHGREEN, so the two sends are identical in every field and both are asserted. The program has 19 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN sites and this single invocation legitimately reaches two of them; the send COUNT is itself behaviour, so expectedResponse carries an ORDERED LIST OF EXACTLY TWO, and a translation that suppressed the duplicate as a tidy-up would differ here (practice B5). expectedMessages is EMPTY, and that is a deliberate assertion rather than an omission: that channel is for lines a program EMITS, which in this codebase means COBOL DISPLAY, and every DISPLAY in COBIL00C - :366, :397, :430, :461, :490 and :541 - sits in a WHEN OTHER arm of a file operation, while this path takes the NORMAL arm of every one of the six RESP-tested operations it performs. The ordered record of BOTH emissions is the ordered pair of sends above, each carrying its own ERRMSGO; repeating the text on a message channel would claim a DISPLAY the program never makes and would be reported as a difference in the emitted-line count. :235 UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE at :377-403 likewise takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :388 of the EVALUATE at :387-403 / CONTINUE and adds no message of its own; in Java it is AccountRepository.rewrite (gate G47). THE 300-BYTE ACCOUNT RECORD, SLICED FROM THE FIXTURE RATHER THAN RECALLED. app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy in declaration order: ACCT-ID 9(11) at 1-11, ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 12, ACCT-CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 at 13-24, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT at 25-36, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT at 37-48, ACCT-OPEN-DATE X(10) at 49-58, the misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) at 59-68, ACCT-REISSUE-DATE X(10) at 69-78, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT at 79-90, ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT at 91-102, ACCT-ADDR-ZIP X(10) at 103-112, ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) at 113-122 and FILLER X(178) at 123-300 - which is 300, the RECLN the copybook's header states (gate G19). ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE IS MISSPELLED IN THE COPYBOOK AT CVACT01Y.cpy:11 AND IS MISSPELLED HERE (requirement I1): correcting it to ACCT-EXPIRATION-DATE would leave the diff looking for a span the decoder never produces, which is a silent parity break rather than a loud one. THE OFFSET TRAP, VERIFIED BY SLICING: offsets 103-112 hold 'A000000000' and that span is ACCT-ADDR-ZIP, while ACCT-GROUP-ID at 113-122 holds TEN SPACES - prose elsewhere describes 'A000000000' as a group-id trailer and it is not, and a case that believed it would pin two fields wrongly while the total still summed to 300. FILLER X(178) IS PINNED, AS 178 SPACES (gate G21). ONLY ACCT-CURR-BAL DIFFERS FROM THE SEEDED ROW, from 00000001940{ to 00000000000{; every other one of the thirteen spans is byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt row 0, which is byte-identical to the shipped src/test/resources/fixtures/acctdata.txt (50 rows of exactly 300 bytes, gate G16), and was taken from it by slicing rather than from memory. WHAT EACH CHANNEL ASSERTS. expectedWrites carries two records in write order: the TRANSACT record the WRITE at :512 added, at write position 0, and the ACCTDAT record the EXEC CICS REWRITE at :379-385 replaced, at write position 0 of its own dataset. expectedFinalState carries three: TRANSACT row 0 is the seeded master row, pinned byte for byte and UNCHANGED, which proves the WRITE added rather than replaced; TRANSACT row 1 is the new transaction, so the row index is 1 because the master held one row before the run and the addition lands after it in key order - 0000000000000008 collates after 0000000000000007; and ACCTDAT row 0 is the rewritten account. The seeded master row is itself what INITIALIZE leaves behind for everything but its identifier - the EXEC CICS READPREV at :474-482 reads only the key from it - so its alphanumeric spans are spaces, its TRAN-CAT-CD and TRAN-MERCHANT-ID are zero-filled, and its TRAN-AMT is the positive zero 0000000000{. expectedDatasets adds the four counts a row-level expectation cannot state: TRANSACT one row on WRITES and two on FINAL_STATE, ACCTDAT one on each, with the widths that identify each dataset, 350 for CVTRA05Y and 300 for CVACT01Y. Every span of every record is pinned BOTH as a named field and inside the complete image - the names make a failure say TRAN-AMT rather than 'offset 132', and the image accounts for every remaining byte and therefore proves the total width and that both FILLER spans were emitted at all. STATELESSNESS, AND THE CONTEXT STAYS 1. EIBCALEN is 218: the 160 bytes app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy declares for CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 58 bytes of the CDEMO-CB00-INFO group COBIL00C.cbl:63-72 appends inside the same 01 group. The area arrives with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT of 1, which is what :112 tests through CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and is the REENTER half of gate G38, and it leaves as 1: no XCTL occurs on this arm, so RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN and its MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT at :280 are never reached and the next invocation re-enters again. All sixteen shared spans travel back exactly as they arrived, because no statement on this path writes one. The whole of the conversation state - the area, the AID and the screen values - travels in the payload, so no server-side session state exists or is implied (gate G37, AAP rule R6), and the termination is the pseudo-conversational EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA). UNIT KIND. SERVICE, driving BillPaymentService.processEnterKey - the real @Service, constructed through its own constructor and called as a plain object, with NO HTTP, no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no application context anywhere in the path (gate G51). That is where the arithmetic of :224 and :234 lives, which is exactly why the service split exists and exactly why the case that asserts it must reach it with nothing in between. The unit of work is real, because :351 states the UPDATE option and a record lock outside a unit of work is released before the REWRITE at :235 can rely on it. Structured control flow throughout, preserving evaluation order and every arm's outcome (AAP rule R7), and the class name comes from the plan while every behaviour above comes from the source (AAP rule R1). Fixed width is the wire format (AAP rule R5): every span above is expressed at its declared byte width and nothing is trimmed. PROVENANCE.
